scopeReview: PSO-6.C.1:rank-size, primate-city dominance, gravity-style interaction, Christaller/central-place hierarchy, threshold, range and functional hinterlands. Models remain conditional, boundaries/units clear and definitions separated.
varietyReview: Four assessed stimuli:primate population bars, missing ideal rank-size entry, gravity-index inputs and original seven-hexagon/local-service diagram. Checks recompute4:1 dominance, rank-three4 million,1000/500 indices and actual rendered hex geometry/center coverage. Further source and application items test thresholds, range and model limits.
repetitionReview: Different hierarchy operations rather than city-name substitutions; all populations/model parameters invented. Hex diagram is a general threshold illustration, explicitly not a strict K=3 reproduction. Numerical tasks independently recomputed; complete option reasoning and varied keys. Difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Official scope and original academic model exposition checked for conceptual limits. No figure, actual urban-system data, official exam question or proprietary ranking copied. All diagram geometry original; no independent human review or new resource.

questions.correctOption: The largest city has four times the second-largest city’s population and stands well above the simple rank-size expectation.
questions.independentReview: Independently checked12/3=4 and rank-two benchmark12/2=6. Chose an unambiguous large disparity, not a contested exact minimum definition of primacy. No welfare or government-function conclusion inferred.
Independently substituted ranks1–4 into12/r, obtaining12,6,4,3. The missing entry is not already shown as a bar value; no rounding or multiple-correct alternative.

questions.correctOption: A’s index is twice B’s despite B’s larger population.
questions.independentReview: Independently recomputed1000 versus500 and ratio2. The common-origin population and proportionality constant are fixed/omitted; units and formula explicitly defined. Not an exact real trip forecast.

questions.correctOption: A larger demand threshold can require a wider customer base, supporting fewer higher-order centers.
questions.independentReview: Verified seven adjoining original local-area hexagons/dots and one H specialty designation; local grocers exist at all seven. No claim the hospital/repair catchment is an exact Christaller K=3 market principle; this is a general threshold/hierarchy illustration.

questions.correctOption: The town can meet the bakery’s threshold but not the specialist’s under the stated assumptions.
questions.independentReview: Compared5000 to2000/50000 directly. Population is stipulated as the proxy for demand in this model; no guarantee every resident purchases or a real business should open/close.

questions.correctOption: Primacy concerns dominance within an urban system; administrative capital status is a separate function that may or may not coincide.
questions.independentReview: No actual capital/primacy case or contested2:1 cutoff used. Distinction is conceptual and aligned with urban hierarchy rather than political trivia.

questions.correctOption: It suggests stronger interaction under the model’s assumptions, but actual flows require data and may differ because of omitted factors.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished a relative model result from measured flows, independent of the numeric comparison item. No universal distance exponent asserted for every empirical gravity application.

questions.correctOption: The range people are willing to travel for different services.
questions.independentReview: Explicitly contrasted range with threshold and avoided assuming Euclidean range guarantees access through every actual network. Fictional preferences, not health travel guidance.

questions.correctOption: Market areas and interactions may be distorted by access differences, so the ideal geometry needs adjustment.
questions.independentReview: Kept multiple competing central places distinct from the one-market vonThünen setup. No exact distorted boundary or actual mountain settlement inferred.

questions.correctOption: The inventory’s coverage and consistent urban definitions may influence the apparent pattern, especially toward lower ranks.
questions.independentReview: Evidence-coverage issue specific to hierarchy testing, not a fabricated national ranking. Does not assert the largest few ranks must change solely because small cities were omitted.

questions.correctOption: Goods, services and customer trips link the center to a surrounding market area, within a wider hierarchy of places.
questions.independentReview: Recognized overlapping functional areas without claiming one rigid catchment for every service. Consistent with model limitations and interdependence in PSO-6.C.1.
